newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline on hold, looks to U.S. for direction.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline on hold, looks to U.S. for direction.

text.p: European gasoline markets went into holding mode on Thursday after falling sharply on Wednesday. Traders said the market was looking to the U.S. for direction after Tuesday's raft of bearish U.S. stock data and demand forecasts from the API.

Prompt gasoline barge prices were initially weaker pressured by hedge related selling. Some traders said the market's short term contango had steadied cargo prices but one pointed out that most of the avails were for early May delivery anyway so there was little pressure on sellers for a quick sale.
"There are several cargoes showing but the short term contango favours the sellers," a trader said. "The market will stay on hold for a while until people see how U.S. demand pans out in May".

Though several cargoes were seen available, traders said the sellers were reluctant to put a price on them due to the current lack of buying interest. Premium unleaded was assessed notionally stable around $196/$197 a tonne cif NWE.
On the key ARA barge market prices for balance of April liftings came under some pressure in early trade with one trade house selling the market lower as a hedge against a swaps position.
A barge loading April 25 was heard sold down to $188.25 a tonne fob ARA nearly $3 under the previous trade. Early May liftings fared slightly better slipping only $1 to trade at $193 a tonne.
